primary_claim: Low-dimensional (single-direction) activation steering can increase or decrease chain-of-thought coherence and faithfulness in a reasoning model finetuned to have misaligned CoT, but has little effect on the unmodified base model.
stated_future_work: Make the steering pipeline more robust and investigate if the observed behaviour persists
Finetune on a much larger and more diverse dataset to reduce overfitting to the training distribution
Identify maximally causal model layers via attribution patching rather than empirical search
Collect a larger dataset of activating vs non-activating examples for faithfulness steering
Use larger models to improve robustness and reduce risk of spurious correlations
limitations_stated: Post-steering outputs were sometimes messy, with incorrect grammar or repeated tokens
Possible overfitting to the finetuning training data rather than learning a general misalignment concept
Very small dataset for the faithfulness experiment (about 50 activating and 50 non-activating examples)
Compute constraints limited experiments to Colab with A100/T4 GPUs
Only 1.5B and 8B models used, limiting robustness of results
quote: I found that it is possible to steer a model into being more or less coherently aligned between its CoT and its final answer tokens.
